title: Show password prompt immediately if lock screen is displayed after a wake-from-sleep
line: After waking from sleep, the lock screen now shows the password field right away instead of just the clock.
explanation: The lock screen starts in the clock-only view and only reveals the password prompt on input, or when the authenticator sends a message. After a resume that only happened if PAM (e.g. fingerprint) answered before the screen came back, so with a password it never did. The lock screen UI now listens to the resumingFromSuspend signal it already gets from SessionManagement and shows the prompt; the usual 10 s fadeout still returns it to the clock view.

commits.message:
lockscreen: show the password prompt after waking from sleep

After resuming, the lock screen only showed the clock, and the prompt
appeared only on input or when PAM happened to send a message in time.
Now it is shown on resume and fades out after the usual timeout.

BUG: 404063

media.caption: Right after resuming (simulated logind PrepareForSleep false): only the clock is shown
Right after resuming: the password prompt is already shown
About 15 s later, with no input: back to the clock view, as before

review.text: Connecting to SessionManagement.resumingFromSuspend in LockScreenUi.qml directly fixes the root cause described in the report and comment 4 instead of relying on PAM message timing. The change is minimal, reuses the existing SessionManagement connection, keeps normal non-suspend locking unchanged, and preserves the standard 10 s fadeout back to the clock view as verified.

reviews.text: Connecting to SessionManagement.resumingFromSuspend in LockScreenUi.qml directly fixes the root cause described in the report and comment 4 instead of relying on PAM message timing. The change is minimal, reuses the existing SessionManagement connection, keeps normal non-suspend locking unchanged, and preserves the standard 10 s fadeout back to the clock view as verified.

Does exactly what Nate asked in c0 and c4: the prompt is always shown on resume, no longer depending on PAM timing, and the standard 10 s fadeout still applies. It uses the existing SessionManagement.resumingFromSuspend signal next to the aboutToSuspend handler already there. Setting uiVisible goes through the same path as a PAM message (requestActivate, fadeout restart, startAuthenticating), so nothing new can go wrong. The evidence uses a dbusmock logind covering resume, the fadeout, a second cycle and a plain lock with no sleep, which is convincing.
